data.name: Rewind
data.detailed_description:
Try. Try again. In Rewind you can clone yourself and manipulate time to solve both the puzzles and the mystery of why you are here. Use the weapons at your disposal to eliminate your enemies, even if it's yourself. Can you make it to the exit? You can only count on yourselves.

Created by Rachel "Angel_Mapper" Cordone, author of the award winning Unreal Tournament 3 mod "Prometheus", Rewind is the debut game from Stubborn Horse Studios.

reviews.review:
I was always a pretty practical kid. When asked what my ideal superpower would be if I had one, my mind would always instantly think of either clones or the ability to control time. Well, what might happen if you could combine [i]both[/i] of those powers? A little puzzle game called Rewind I suppose.

[h1]The Breakdown[/h1]
[i]Antichamber[/i]. [i]The Ball[/i]. [i]Colortone[/i]. What do these games all have in common? Well, they're a helluva' lot like a little obscure game called Portal. We've all probably heard of it by now. If you somehow haven't though, it's a first-person puzzle platformer from almost a decade ago (wow, it's weird to think that!). It came out at a perfect time, when pretty much nothing like it was on the market, besides similar mods for other games. Well, flash forward nearly a decade later and it seems like the "Portal-esque genre of first-person puzzlers is starting to become more and more saturated. FPPs (I'm lazy so that's what I'll call them) come out all the time, so what makes this one unique?

Well, it's fresh and brings some interesting ideas to the table. See, Rewind works off of the notion that it's a co-op game that you play by yourself. The game gives you the tools to solve multi-player puzzles in the form of 2 extra clones and the ability to manipulate time. You can't fast forward at all, but you certainly are able to "rewind" to correct mistakes or move back to the start so you can use a different clone - hence, the game's title.

Now, normally I'm skeptical of games that rely off of a single gimmick, but [i]Rewind[/i] quickly subdued my worries. Similar to 2007's Portal, I was instantly engrossed by not only the central mechanic of the game, but also its setting. Upon starting the game, you're thrust into an unfamiliar laboratory-type area with little to no explanation about your surroundings. Even by the end of the game, it's still pretty ambiguous in regards to when and where this game takes place. Why am I here? And who is that guy who talks to my character between rooms? 

Most questions, narrative-wise, that I had with Rewind were never answered while playing, and that's kind of a shame. I feel as if the game wanted to provide this immensely interesting sci-fi story to complement its unique gameplay but just wasn't able to in the time provided. Only one major event really happens in the story (besides an event that occurred prior the start of the game), and it's at the very end anyway. None of it is explained either, though I think I admittedly did miss a possible alternate ending that could have fleshed out the story slightly more. 

See, the way that the game works is that each level has one solution (generally pretty simple, or at least straightforward). Once you reach the solution, the door opens and you continue onwards to the next level. However, the final level has [i]two[/i] solutions from what I understand, so I think each one leads to a different ending. I breezed past most of the game, but for some reason the final level really stumped me. It got me stuck for about a half hour or so, which was about 1/6 of my total playtime actually, considering the game is only about 3 hours long. What I assume is the "bad ending" is hard enough to get, but to reach (what I assume is) the "good ending" takes some extra brain cells that I'm just probably lacking. Perhaps one day I'll go back and get the other ending, but for now I'll leave an ambiguous "???" when it comes to what I can make of the story of the game.

In terms of Rewind's visuals, it's nothing spectacular, but the textures, lighting, and designs of the main characters and enemies (which are only there for puzzle purposes) do their job decently I suppose. It's an Unreal Engine game, so of course that's to be expected. Sound-wise, the game has two voice actors actually - both do fine jobs, though again, nothing exceptional. The music for the game is similarly "eh". It does its job; nothing more and nothing less.

So, despite all my negative criticisms, why am I still recommending Rewind? Well, perhaps it's to make a statement: make more unique games like this! That goes out to anyone, not just the developer (who is mostly only one person I think!) of this game. Perhaps it's also because the concept of mixing time manipulation with clones is just right up my alley. However, perhaps more than anything it's because this game is actually fairly good. Sure, there's some problems, but I think overall Rewind is at least something a little special, and hey - it's pretty fun too!

[h1]Pros[/h1]
[list]
[*]Unique mix of time-manipulation and cloning mechanics to solve creative yet straightforward puzzles.
[*]Extra replayability in the form of Time Trials and Clone Trials - two modes that add an extra challenge to the normal levels.
[*]49 levels total (42 without the 7 tutorial levels)
[*]Decent variety of game mechanics: clones, time manipulation, guns (or rather 1 gun), enemies, elevators, moving platforms, switches, appearing/disappearing platforms, etc.
[*]Mysterious story revolving around the main character waking up in a mysterious facility.
[*]Steam achievements.
[/list]

[h1]Cons[/h1]
[list]
[*]Short length - only 3 hours long or so!
[*]The game is generally pretty easy, or at least definitely very straightforward in its level design. Each level uses only a small handful of mechanics to get you to the exit.
[*]The visuals, voice acting, and music certainly aren't incredible, but they do their job just fine.
[*]Story is very simple and doesn't really go anywhere; nor does it explain most of the questions I had at all. Expect very little plot-wise.
[*]Little to no secrets as far as I could tell. Kind of disappointed about that.
[/list]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Rewind is a fun, unique first-person puzzle platformer with a very unique mechanic. Nothing about is particularly exceptional besides that, yet the game itself is still pretty enjoyable, and for that fact alone I'd give it a solid recommendation.


[h1][b]Final Verdict: 7/10[/b][/h1]
